title: Two Sum
statement: Given a list `nums` and an integer `target`, return the two indices `[i, j]` (with `i < j`) such that `nums[i] + nums[j] == target`. Exactly one solution is guaranteed. Return the indices as a sorted list `[i, j]`.

predict_steps.prompt: nums=[2,7,11,15], target=9. At i=0 you see 2. What complement do you look for?
When i reaches 1, nums[1] is 7. Which earlier index pairs with it?

viva.question: What is the time cost of a hash-map Two Sum versus checking every pair?
expected_points: a single pass is linear time with a hash map
each map lookup is amortized constant time

viva.question: What breaks if a solution reuses the same index for both addends?
expected_points: the problem requires two distinct indices
a value that appears once cannot pair with itself
i must stay strictly less than j
self-pairs violate the statement even when 2*x equals target

viva.question: Why must you record seen values while scanning instead of after the whole pass?
expected_points: the complement may already appear earlier in the array
the map stores value-to-index for the prefix seen so far
waiting until the end loses the chance to match on the fly
one forward scan is enough once past values are remembered
